Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: yomal321
Message:
Fix login 500 in uat: wire up the missing SESSION_SECRET

Same bug dev hit (PR 868): SESSION_SECRET was never sealed for vega-uat, so
every login got past password verification, failed to sign the session JWT,
and surfaced as a bare Internal server error. Sealed a fresh, uat-specific
SESSION_SECRET offline with kubeseal (never reused dev's value — sealed
secrets are namespace-bound anyway) and wired it into values-uat.yaml.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: yomal321
Message:
Fix login 500: wire up the missing SESSION_SECRET

vega-web never had SESSION_SECRET set on this cluster -- only
DATABASE_URL was wired. Every login got past password verification,
then threw signing the session ("SESSION_SECRET is 0 bytes; at least
32 are required"), surfaced to the browser as a bare Internal server
error. AZURE_DEPLOYMENT.md documents the same requirement for the
Azure target; it was just never carried over here.

Sealed offline against the shipped public cert (no cluster access
needed for this part) as a new vega-app-secrets SealedSecret, kept
separate from vega-db-credentials since it isn't a DB credential.
Per sealed-secrets/README.md this chart doesn't render sealed-secrets/
via ArgoCD, so vega-app-secrets-dev.yaml still needs a manual
`kubectl apply -f` by whoever has write access before this env var
will actually resolve.

Also confirmed the seed Job that ran under the previous commit worked
(login got as far as "Invalid email or password") and disarmed
runDbSeed, per the plan in that commit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Yomal Theekshana
Message:
Add sealed vega-db-credentials for vega-dev

Sealed offline against sealing-cert.pem (username, password, DATABASE_URL).
The vega-web deployment and vega-infra postgresql templates already
reference this secret name, but it was never sealed/applied, leaving both
vega-web and vega-postgresql-0 stuck in CreateContainerConfigError.

Nothing in the chart renders this file -- ArgoCD does not apply it.
DevOps needs to kubectl apply it in vega-dev; see
deploy/helm/sealed-secrets/README.md "Applying".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
